$comment: GDAL native stack for the win_arm64 wheel (#334), built by ci/setup-gdal-from-vcpkg.ps1
on the windows-11-arm runner. The feature list mirrors the curated driver contract
asserted by ci/verify-wheel.py (default features are OFF to drop
postgresql/libkml/spatialite/libxml2, matching the Linux from-source curation).
NOTE: the vcpkg gdal port has no hdf4 feature, so the arm64 wheel shares the Linux
wheel's HDF4 gap.
The manifest 'version' field is required by vcpkg but unused by this build and is NOT
commitizen-managed - it stays 0 permanently.
The 'overrides' below pin EXACT port versions at resolve time (mirroring the canonical
pins in ci/source-build/config.sh where the ecosystems allow): a builtin-baseline move
can never silently change these - vcpkg either builds the pinned version or fails.
Bumping = update the override AND expect a cold rebuild (new cache key).
name: pyramids-core

$comment: gdal pulls hdf5 in transitively for its hdf5/netcdf features, and vcpkg builds it
with HDF5_ENABLE_THREADSAFE=OFF by default. A non-threadsafe HDF5 may not be
entered from more than one OS thread over the process lifetime, so dask threaded
reads segfault inside GDAL OpenMDArray (#1620). Naming hdf5 explicitly here is
what carries the feature: features are unioned per port, so gdal still gets the
same build. The port maps threadsafe -> HDF5_ENABLE_THREADSAFE and implicitly
sets HDF5_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED=ON because hl is also built, which is the combination
libnetcdf needs. This file is in the vcpkg cache key, so the change rebuilds.
dependencies.name: hdf5
